thread:
maria: FYI customer Lucy is hitting persistent 429s on Dedicated despite reserved capacity. They say traffic is being routed to shared-default and autoscale never kicked. Customer: lucy@acme.com, tenant_id=acme-42, request sample id=req_0a1b2c

lucy (customer): We're getting 429s every ~10s bursts, latency spikes, and our dashboard shows requests to shared-default pool. We bought gold dedicated, this started after yesterday's control-plane deploy.

maria: Repro steps from customer: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "X-Redwood-Tier: gold" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -> 429, response header X-Redwood-Pool: shared-default

maria: Attached snippet of control-plane routing log they captured: 
```
2026-03-15T10:12:34Z controlplane routing eval tenant=acme-42 headers={"x-redwood-tier":"gold", "x-tenant-affinity":"acme-42"} -> policy-match default-pool (score 0.62)
```

jonas (eng-oncall): Assigned. Can you paste the full request headers and the exact X-Redwood-Tier value? Also need the tenant config (policy set) for acme-42.

maria: Full headers from customer (sanitized): 
```
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
X-Redwood-Tier: ["gold"]
X-Tenant-Affinity: acme-42
User-Agent: acme-service/1.2.3
```

ashok (eng-routing): Hmm they're sending X-Redwood-Tier as a JSON array string (we expect tokenized single value). Routing parser has special-case that flattens arrays by taking first element but there was a recent normalization change that trims quotes differently and can convert it to literal string of brackets. If header arrives as "[\"gold\"]" we treat it as unknown tier. That would cause fallback to default-pool and avoid dedicated autoscale.

jonas (eng-oncall): Can reproduce locally by sending header exactly as customer did. Repro steps: 
```
curl -H 'X-Redwood-Tier: ["gold"]' -H 'X-Tenant-Affinity: acme-42' ...
# controlplane logs: policy lookup got tier='["gold"]' which doesn't match 'gold' rule
```

ashok (eng-routing): Root cause: controlplane header-normalization routine introduced in 2026-03-14 will JSON-decode a header if it looks like array but then don't strip outer spacing. For headers with quotes/encodings we end up with value containing brackets. Policy matcher does strict equality.

maria: Customer insists they didn't change anything; their HTTP client upgraded lib last week and now sends tier as array. Ops should handle both.

jonas (eng-oncall): Immediate mitigation: update policy matcher to use fuzzy match for tier (strip non-alphanum) and allow array-first-element extraction. Pushing a hotfix to staging now. Also temporary workaround: create tenant rule mapping for "[\"gold\"]" -> gold-pool to unblock customer.

ashok (eng-routing): Working on two PRs: 1) normalization fix (safe: trim brackets/quotes and collapse arrays) 2) tolerant matcher fallback when dedicated rule exists for tenant. Will add tests. ETA ~60 minutes.

ella (billing): Heads up — customer flagged potential billing discrepancy; they've been charged shared pool rates for last 12 hours. If we misrouted, we should credit at dedicated rate differential. Assign to billing ops if hotfix doesn't land in next 2 hours.

sre-bot: Deploy job queued: controlplane-normalize-array-headers-v1 -> canary -> rollout. CI: 4/4 passing.

jonas (eng-oncall): Canary applied to region us-west-2. I validated with same curl payload: now X-Redwood-Pool returns acme-gold and 200 OK. Autoscale fired (observed replica scale from 1->3).

maria: Confirmed with customer — Lucy reports 200s and no throttling after canary. They've accepted the tenant mapping rollback is not required.

ashok (eng-routing): Merged both PRs to main with tests. Postmortem ticket created: PM-4782. Notes: add header-schema docs, warn about client libs sending arrays, and add mapping telemetry metric.

ella (billing): I'll prepare a one-off credit for the window we misrouted. Will follow up with Lucy with amount.

maria: Closing loop with customer and marked incident resolved. Will link logs & PRs in support ticket. :white_check_mark:
